finding.claim: /fetch2 forwards an unvalidated user-supplied URL to requests.get with redirects enabled; only the URL scheme is checked, so internal hosts, loopback, and cloud metadata endpoints are reachable and the first 200 bytes of the response are returned to the caller.
finding.sink: views.py:22 requests.get(url, timeout=5) — server-side outbound HTTP request; response body returned in JSON

trace.note: url taken from query string, no normalization
is_http_url called as the only guard
is_http_url checks only urlparse(url).scheme in (http, https); no host/IP check
requests.get called with same unvalidated url; allow_redirects defaults to True so 3xx to internal targets are followed
first 200 chars of body reflected in response

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist only (validators.py:7). No host, IP-range, port, or redirect restriction. Name is_http_url suggests more than it checks.

verdict.guard_found: None on the /fetch2 path. views.py:20 calls is_http_url, which at validators.py:7 checks only urlparse(url).scheme in ("http", "https"). No host, IP, or redirect check precedes requests.get at views.py:22, and it uses default allow_redirects. The stronger is_safe_url (validators.py:10-18) is imported at views.py:4 but is not called on /fetch2. The /fetch route at views.py:12 and :14 does use it with allow_redirects=False, so that route is not affected.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled url at views.py:19 reaches requests.get at views.py:22 after only a scheme check (validators.py:7 via views.py:20), with no host or IP restriction and redirects followed by default, and the first 200 bytes of the response are returned at views.py:22.

finding.claim: /fetch validates the destination by resolving the hostname once, then fetches the URL with requests.get which resolves it again. A DNS-rebinding domain can return a public IP at check time and an internal IP at connect time, bypassing the private/loopback/link-local/reserved check.
finding.sink: views.py:14 requests.get(url, timeout=5, allow_redirects=False) — server-side outbound request; response body returned in JSON

trace.note: scheme must be http/https and hostname must be non-empty
socket.getaddrinfo(hostname, port or 443) — first DNS resolution; port defaults to 443 even for http://
each returned address parsed by ipaddress.ip_address
rejects is_private, is_loopback, is_link_local, is_reserved; all addresses must pass
requests.get resolves hostname again independently; no IP pinning between check and connect

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist (validators.py:12); all resolved addresses checked (validators.py:14-17); allow_redirects=False (views.py:14) closes redirect bypass; timeout=5 does not limit destination. Confidence medium-high: relies on attacker-controlled DNS with short TTL; not run against live DNS.

verdict.guard_found: No closing guard. The scheme check (validators.py:12) and the private/loopback/link-local/reserved IP check (validators.py:14-17) are not among the accepted closers, since neither is an exact hostname allowlist. allow_redirects=False (views.py:14) addresses redirects, not DNS rebinding. Nothing pins the resolved IP between validators.py:14 and views.py:14.
verdict.reason: The check at validators.py:14-17 and the fetch at views.py:14 each resolve the hostname independently with no IP pinning, and the hostname comes straight from the unauthenticated query string at views.py:11, so a rebinding DNS record can pass the check and then reach an internal address. Also, /fetch2 at views.py:19-22 has no IP check at all, so it is a more direct SSRF than the candidate describes and was not mentioned in the candidate.
